proposals.evidence: Platts p. 1103 labels mahīnā “month” Persian/Hindi and analyzes mah/māh plus -īna. The explicit h-bearing and transparent h-loss variants are kept together; highly contracted mina/mena need separate local evidence. Existing Hindi mahina “month” (kannauji[p. 85]) supplies an attested provisional donor. Its locality is the attestation site; the historical lending locality and possible intervening Indo-Aryan language remain unknown. The borrowed edge is saved under the user’s explicit preference to link supported families despite unresolved cross-IA transmission.
